title: Native cross-host mailbox reads return 503 "central mailbox response unavailable" while a full gate loads the central host
outcome: A satellite participant's native mailbox read (and a reply append) through the central host stays available and gives a definite answer while a full test gate runs on the central host. Reading a page never depends on a persist-writer deadline that gate load routinely misses. If the receipt issuance must be durable, the read returns the page with a typed "receipt pending, retry with the same key" answer within budget, not a bare 503 with an unknown outcome.
acceptance: The holder's note names, with file:line locators, the code path by which a satellite's native mailbox read is proxied to the central host and why it returns 503 'central mailbox response unavailable; central mailbox outcome may be unknown' under gate load. It also names which durable write (e.g. receipt issuance) the read waits on, and its deadline. It correlates the 2026-10-20 occurrences: the O1-Mac read at about 16:24:45Z and the reply append at about 16:14:45Z, both during the CSharpProof full gate test-899d1493.
A fail-first test reproduces a native mailbox read through the central host while the persist writer is slow (a controlled delay seam, not real load) and shows today's 503 or unknown outcome.

With the fix, under that same slow-writer seam, the read returns the page within the documented budget, either with an issued receipt or with a typed, retry-safe 'receipt pending' answer that a retry with the same key resolves to the same page (within one central process incarnation; after a central restart a same-key retry returns a typed readKeyExpired and the client reads afresh under a new key). A reply append under the same seam gives a definite committed or not-committed answer. Tests cover both.
The full five-stage gate passes on the exact committed tree, and an independent review pair has no outstanding in-scope Medium-or-higher finding.
